name: Hypertechno
summary: Hard-techno-derived 4/4 kick at 145–160 with the energy moved onto the offbeat 8th: a monolithic sidechained bass stab (often a hardstyle reverse bass) and an open hat between every kick, a big clean clap on 2 and 4 (or every beat) with eurodance flams, and punchy, undistorted drums built for phone speakers. Unlike hard techno it keeps pop structure and uses hard-dance snare rolls, clap-doubling builds, kick drop-outs and half-bar silences before the drop.

sounds.kick: Clean, short, clicky peak-time techno kick (909 layered with a sine sub, or a designed Kick 2 kick) hard-clipped rather than distortion-stacked; the offbeat bass owns the low end between hits.
sounds.snare: Big 909+808 clap stack with a short room as the signature backbeat, a 2000s dance snare (909 / Alesis SR-16) doubling it in choruses, a bright pitched snare for rolls, 909/707 rim for pickup skips.
sounds.hats: 909 open hat on every offbeat 8th (hands-up heritage), clean 909/707 closed 16ths between with the offbeat 16th emphasised, Korg EMX hats for a brighter synthetic edge; bright and uncompressed.
sounds.percussion: Synthetic 909/Simmons toms for eurodance bounce and tom-fall risers, 16th shaker or tambourine in the peak-time lane, Virus TI noise impacts; almost no organic percussion.
sounds.cymbals: Crash on every drop downbeat and phrase start; soft ride 8ths only in the peak-time-derived lane.

machines: Roland TR-909 — kick base, clap, open/closed hats, toms, ride (owned)
Roland TR-808 — clap layer under the 909 clap (owned)
Roland TR-707 — clean closed hats and rim (owned)
Alesis SR-16 / D4 — 2000s dance snare layer for choruses (owned)
Yamaha RX11 — bright pitched snare for snare-roll builds (owned)
Korg Electribe EMX — bright synthetic hats and claps (owned)
Simmons SDS — synthetic toms for the eurodance bounce and tom-fall risers (owned)
Novation Drumstation / Quasimidi 309 — clicky 909-style kicks and rave claps (owned)
Virus TI — noise sweeps and impact hits for drops (owned)
Sonic Academy Kick 2 — designed clean kicks used in most tutorials (get elsewhere)
